__init__.py in vendor/gguf/ is NOT vendored from upstream. It is a minimal
stub written for this project, because upstream's real __init__.py does
`from .gguf_writer import *`, `from .metadata import *`, `from .vocab import *`,
etc. across the whole package, which we did not vendor and do not need.
Import the reader directly as `from gguf.gguf_reader import GGUFReader`.

Reason for pinning to a commit instead of `pip install gguf`: the upstream
gguf-py package changes weekly (see hardening commits below), and this
project's tests and FINDINGS.md cite specific line numbers in gguf_reader.py.
`pip install gguf` would silently drift the line numbers out from under the
citations on the next `pip install --upgrade`.

Hardening history confirmed present in this vendored snapshot (all three
were re-checked by grep against the vendored file, see project FINDINGS.md
for exact line numbers at this commit):

  - 418dea39ce (2026-02-24, PR #19856): alignment must be a non-zero power
    of two, else ValueError.
  - 5788b510a1 (2026-08-04, PR #25401, fixes #25378): tensor n_dims must not
    exceed GGML_MAX_DIMS (4), else ValueError.
  - 0329fcdac8 (2026-08-19, PR #27188): size guards on kv_count, tensor_count,
    string length, and array length, all bounded by 1024*1024*1024 (GGUF_MAX_
    STRING_LENGTH / GGUF_MAX_ARRAY_ELEMENTS), else ValueError.

Do not modify these vendored files. If the fuzzer finds a bug, report it in
FINDINGS.md; do not patch the vendored source to work around it.
